 -3-  NC: 2024:KHC:1705  MFA No. 2420 of 2018  JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the Insurance Company under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for short), challenging the judgment and award passed in MVC No.804/2015 dated 05.12.2017 by the Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mysuru praying to reduce the quantum of compensation on the ground that the deceased was aged 71 years old and the Tribunal has erred in adding 15% to his income towards loss of future prospects in life.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The factum of accident, injuries sustained by the claimant and coverage of insurance are not in dispute.

3. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the records.
4.

In the present case, the Tribunal has awarded compensation as under:
NC: 2024:KHC:1705 1
Towards Loss of financial Rs.7,17,876/- dependency 2 Towards loss of love and affection Rs.40,000/- 3

Towards estate Rs.15,000/-
4 Towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- transportation of body 5 Towards loss of consortium Rs.40,000/-
In the present case, the Tribunal has added 15% of income towards loss of future prospects in life.

As per judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 2700, the deceased, who are above the age of 60 years are not entitled for addition of income towards loss of future prospects in life.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. The deceased was a retired bank employee and was getting monthly pension of Rs.15,808/- and he was also working as a Manager at Journey Bag Company after retirement and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Learned counsel for the claimants has produced Ex.P.13 - salary certificate of Journey Bag Company.
He was aged NC: 2024:KHC:1705 about 71 years old at the time of the accident.
Considering the age of the deceased, he would have earned an amount of Rs.5,000/- per month for working as a Manager at Journey Bag Company.
Hence, the monthly income of the deceased can be taken into consideration as Rs.15,808/- + 5,000/- = Rs.20,808/- per month.
The claimant No.1 is the wife of the deceased.
The other claimants are major children, who are not entitled for compensation under the head 'loss of dependency'.
The claimant Nos.2 and 3 being major children and married and are residing separately.
But, claimant No.1 being wife of the deceased is entitled for compensation under the head 'loss of dependency'.
Just because wife is the only dependent on the deceased, 50% of income of deceased cannot be deducted.
But 1/3rd income ought to be deducted.
Considering the age of the deceased at 71 years, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '5'.
1/3rd of his income has to be deducted towards personal expenses.
Therefore, the 'Loss of Dependency' is re-
assessed and quantified as under:

Accordingly, a sum of Rs.8,32,320/- is awarded under the head 'loss of dependency'.

3 7.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co Ltd vs Smt Manjula on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has granted compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head 'loss of love and affection', which is just and proper.

As the children are major and married,
the compensation is awarded only to the wife of the deceased.
The loss of love and affection and loss of consortium are more or less having similar connotations.
Therefore, the compensation of Rs.40,000/- awarded by the Tribunal under the head 'loss of consortium' is kept intact.
8. As per the dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Rasmita Biswal vs. Div. Manager, National Insurance Co., Ltd., reported in AIR 2022 SC 85, for every three years 10% income is to be raised.

entities.text: Rasmita Biswal vs. Div. Manager, National Insurance Co., Ltd., reported in AIR 2022 SC 85
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has granted a sum of Rs.15,000/- each towards 'Funeral expenses' and 'Loss of estate'.

It is just and reasonable to award a sum of Rs.16,500/- each under NC: 2024:KHC:1705 the head 'Transportation of dead body, funeral expenses, etc.,' and 'Loss of estate'.
9.

Thus, in all, the appellants/claimants are entitled for total compensation under various heads as follows:
1 Loss of dependency Rs. 7,17,876/- 8,32,320/-
2 Loss of love and  affection Rs. 40,000/- -
3 Towards loss of estate Rs. 15,000/- 16,500/-
4 Towards funeral  expenses and  transportation of body Rs. 15,000/- 16,500/-
5 Towards loss of  consortium Rs. 40,000/- 40,000/-
 TOTAL Rs. 8,27,876/- 9,05,320/-
10.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.8,27,876/-, but the appellants/claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.9,05,320/-.

Hence, the appellants/claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.77,444/-
(Rs.9,05,320/- -
Rs.8,27,876/-).

Therefore, the appellants/claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.77,444/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of NC: 2024:KHC:1705 petition till the date of realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

11. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed-in-part.
ii.

The impugned judgment and award dated 05.12.2017 in MVC No.804/2015 passed by the Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
The United India Insurance Co Ltd vs Smt Manjula on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112102429/
4 Mysuru, is modified to the extent that the appellants/claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.77,444/-
along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization,
in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
